steps: Open the door and look at the bottom of the dishwasher. If there's standing water, scoop out what you can with a cup and soak the rest up with a towel so you can see the base clearly.

In the base there's a round filter that lifts out by hand — usually a quarter turn to unlock. Take it out, rinse it under the tap to clear any food or grease, and put it back, turning it until it locks.
Have a look at the spray arms — the plastic arms with small holes that spin inside. Check the holes aren't blocked with debris; most unclip by hand so you can rinse them.
Run the kitchen sink tap for a minute and see whether the sink itself drains away normally.
Run a short cycle and listen near the end for a humming or buzzing sound as it tries to drain, then open it and see whether the water has gone.
output.diagnostic_question: After cleaning the filter and running a short cycle — did the water drain away, and did you hear any humming or buzzing sound near the end of the cycle?
output.safety_note: Don't pull the dishwasher out or tilt it, don't undo any screws or panels, and don't touch wiring or the plug beyond checking it's switched on. Don't reach into hot water — let it cool to hand temperature first. If you see water on the floor underneath the machine, water near a socket, or smell burning, stop and tell us straight away.

steps: Have a towel and a shallow bowl ready on the floor in front of the machine first — water will come out. Then look for the small flap at the bottom front of the machine; it opens by hand, or with a coin turn. Open it, let the water drain into the bowl, and tell me what you find behind it (coins, hair grips, fluff, gunk).
Clear anything you find out by hand, close it back up firmly, and run a short rinse cycle. Tell me whether the water clears at the end and whether the door opens.
While that cycle is draining, stand close and listen. Tell me whether you hear a humming or buzzing sound from the machine, or complete silence.

If the back of the machine is already visible without moving it, look at the hose running out of it and tell me whether it looks kinked, squashed or trapped. Please don't pull or tilt the machine to see.
Run the kitchen sink tap for a moment and tell me whether the sink drains away normally or is slow.
output.diagnostic_question: After clearing the flap and running a short rinse cycle, did the water drain away fully — and if not, did you hear any humming from the machine while it was trying to drain, or was it silent?
output.safety_note: Please don't move, tilt or pull out the machine, don't remove any panels or screws, and don't reach into the drum. If any water is hot, leave it. Stop straight away and tell me if you notice a burning smell, smoke, water coming from underneath the machine, or water anywhere near a socket.

Check the plug is pushed firmly into its socket and the socket switch is on. Please don't touch anything at the fuse board.
Stand quietly by the fridge for a moment with the door shut and tell me whether you can hear a low hum or buzz from it — and whether it's constant or comes and goes.

steps: First, tell me whether your hood vents outside through a pipe, or whether it blows the air back into the kitchen. And with the hood running, which speed setting is it on? If it's on the lowest, try turning it up to the highest and see if the steam clears better.

Next, the metal grease filters — these are the mesh panels on the underside of the hood. Each one has a small catch or handle you can release by hand. Take one out and have a look: if it's greasy or clogged, that's very likely the cause. They can be washed in hot soapy water or in a dishwasher, then dried fully and put back.

If your hood blows air back into the kitchen rather than outside, it will also have a carbon filter that can't be washed and needs replacing. Can you tell me roughly when that was last changed, or if you're not sure, just say so.

If your hood vents outside, have a look at the vent on the outside wall from a window or doorway, if you can see it safely from ground level. With the hood running, does the flap open? Just tell me what you see — no need to go near it.
With the hood switched on, stand close and tell me what you can hear: a strong fan noise, a weak or straining noise, or no motor sound at all.
output.diagnostic_question: After cleaning and refitting the grease filters, run the hood on its highest setting while boiling a kettle underneath — does it clear the steam any better than before?
output.safety_note: Please don't climb on a chair, worktop or step to reach the hood, and don't remove any screws, panels or the ducting. Only take out the filters that release by hand. Don't handle water hotter than you'd comfortably wash in, and switch the hood off at its wall switch before removing filters. If you notice a burning smell, smoke or sparking at any point, stop straight away and tell me.

steps: Have a look at the front burner and tell me which bits sit on top — there's usually a flat metal or enamel cap, and underneath it a ring with small slots around the edge. Both lift off by hand when the hob is completely cold.
With the hob cold and all the controls off, lift the cap and ring off the front burner. Check they're dry and that nothing's sitting under them — spills, crumbs or water are common after cooking.
Wipe both parts dry with a cloth and put them back, making sure the cap sits flat and level, not tilted or overhanging. It should feel seated rather than rocking.
Try lighting the front burner again as you normally would, and watch what happens for a few seconds.
If it lights, look at the flame colour and tell me what you see — a steady blue flame is what we want.
output.diagnostic_question: After drying and reseating the cap and ring, does the front burner light — and if it does, is the flame steady blue, or yellow/orange at all?
output.safety_note: This is a gas appliance, so reseating the cap and ring by hand is the only thing you should do — please don't touch the ignition part, the small jet in the middle, the gas supply or the connection behind the hob, and don't use any tools. Only do this when the hob is completely cold. If you smell gas at any point, don't try to light it again: turn the hob off, open a window, avoid switches, and tell us straight away. Stop using the burner and let us know if the flame looks yellow or orange, if you see soot on your pans, or if you notice a burning smell — those need an engineer.

steps: Can you tell me whether the hob is gas (with flames), ceramic (flat glass with glowing rings) or induction (flat glass, only heats when a pan is on it)? A photo of the hob and its controls is helpful too.

If it's ceramic or induction: check the control panel for a key or padlock symbol. If one is showing, turn the hob off, then follow the unlock instructions marked on the panel and tell me if the symbol clears.

If it's induction: hold a fridge magnet against the base of the pan you normally use on those two rings. If it doesn't stick firmly, the pan won't heat — try a pan the magnet does grip, and check the pan base covers most of the ring.
If it's ceramic or induction and still nothing: check the cooker switch on the wall is switched on, and tell me whether other kitchen sockets and appliances are working normally.
If it's gas: don't touch anything on the hob. Just tell me which burners light, what colour the flame is, and whether you can hear clicking when you turn them.
output.diagnostic_question: After trying the checks for your type of hob, do those two rings now heat normally — and if not, what exactly happens when you turn them on?
output.safety_note: If the hob is gas, do not attempt any checks beyond looking and describing — gas work is legally restricted to registered engineers. The one exception is lifting off a burner cap by hand to dry and reseat it flat. Do not remove panels, touch wiring, or reset anything at the fuse box. If you smell gas, see yellow or orange flames, sooting on pans, smoke or a burning smell, stop using the hob immediately and tell me straight away.

steps: First, tell me which kind of hob it is: does it light with a flame (gas), or is it a flat glass surface you wipe over (electric or induction)? A photo of the hob top and the controls would help.

If it's a flat glass hob, check the controls for a small key or padlock symbol — that's a child lock. If it's showing, hold the lock button down for a few seconds until it clears, then try the two rings again.

If it's a flat glass hob and still nothing on those two rings, hold a fridge magnet against the base of the pan you normally use. If it doesn't stick firmly, that pan won't work on some zones — try a different pan and tell me what happens.
If it's a gas hob, don't touch anything on it. Just tell me what you see on the two rings that aren't right: do they light at all, and is the flame blue, or yellow/orange?
If it's a gas hob and the rings do light, you can lift the burner caps off by hand when they're completely cold, dry them with a cloth, and sit them back down flat. Nothing else on a gas hob.
output.diagnostic_question: After trying the step that applies to your hob, do the two rings heat now — and are the other rings still working normally?
output.safety_note: Please don't take anything apart, remove screws, or touch anything to do with the gas supply, jets or ignition — gas work is legally restricted to registered engineers.
